topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: This is the common name for the Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance program.
question.text: What federal program provides income to millions of retired people?
question.clue: Black-dominated professions were originally excluded from this program, which was amended in 1965 to create Medicare and Medicaid.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the namesakes of airports around the world.
swap.text: This former New York City mayor is the namesake of an airport which Joe Biden compared to a "third world country".
swap.answerHtml: Fiorello La Guardia [or Fiorello Henry La Guardia or Fiorello Enrico La Guardia]
swap.clue: While in Congress, this man worked with George Norris to co-sponsor an act that banned yellow-dog contracts.

question.leadin: Give the following about attempts to ease the Great Depression.
question.text: This 1933 law, named for two Democratic senators, created the FDIC. It also notably forbade commercial banks from many investment activities, a measure repealed in 1999.
question.answerHtml: Glass-Steagall Act (prompt on "Banking Act of 1933;” accept logical equivalents for Act, including Bill and Law)
question.clue: Support for it came from a New York City prosecutor named Ferdinand Pecora, and one of its namesakes was a Virginia Senator who later served as Truman's Secretary of the Treasury.

swap.text: The Great Depression led to the election of Franklin Roosevelt, whose thrity nightly radio addresses from 1933 to 1934 were given this name due to their intimate and calming nature.
swap.clue: Similar speeches were given while their speaker was Governor of New York.

question.text: This 1930 tariff raised taxes on about 20,000 goods and led to a decline in U.S. trade, contributing to the Great Depression.
question.clue: Franklin Delano Roosevelt signed the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934 as a direct Democratic response to this Republican legislation.

swap.text: The New Deal included this 1933 law that allowed the President to regulate industry. Its constitutionality was debated in the case Schechter ("SHECK-ter") Poultry Corp. v. United States. It was ultimately struck down.
swap.clue: It set up an agency headed by General Hugh S. Johnson that, and it reduced maximum hours so that more people couple be employed, while its Section 7a was an important concession to labor unions.

question.text: This largest New Deal agency headed by Harry Hopkins built public parks, bridges, roads and other structures.
question.clue: One branch of this organization was led by Hallie Flanagan, under whose leadership that branch undertook news reenactments called the "Living Newspaper," series, while another branch of this organization was responsible for producing the American Guide Series.

swap.leadin: Wilhelm Loeser helped this man disguise himself by giving him plastic surgery and trying to obliterate his fingerprints with acid.
swap.text: Name this Depression-era gangster and bank robber. He was infamously betrayed to federal agents by Ana Cumpanas, the "Woman in Red."
swap.clue: In 1316, one Pope of this name became the second Avignon Pope, succeeding Clement V, while in 1410, one Pope by this name declared the Medici family official bankers to the papacy.

question.text: This military-style employment program paid men thirty dollars a month to maintain forests.
question.clue: Employees of this organization were organized into camps and often lived in tents.

swap.text: This doctor, another critic of FDR's New Deal, popularized a namesake national pension plan which influenced the Social Security Act.
swap.clue: This physician developed a plan for state-funded old-age pensions as a way to stimulate economic spending during the Depression. While FDR eventually adopted the Social Security Act, this man was not pleased with the conservative changes the President made to his proposal.

question.leadin: His book My First Days in the White House was published after his assassination.
question.text: Identify this populist politician assassinated by Karl Weiss, nicknamed "The Kingfisher."
question.clue: This ally of Father Charles Coughlin promoted socialist reforms in his Share the Wealth campaign which promised to make "every man a king."

swap.leadin: Note to Players: A description is acceptable for the first part. Handwriting analysis helped convict Bruno Hauptmann for the kidnapping of this person.
swap.text: Name or describe this child whose 1932 kidnapping and murder led to a "Trial of the Century" and the passage of the Federal Kidnapping Act.
swap.answerHtml: Charles Augustus Lindbergh Jr. [accept answers describing Charles Lindbergh’s son, accept the Lindbergh baby]

question.leadin: Identify the following female senators from American history.
question.text: The widow of an Arkansan senator shocked her colleagues after using an invitation to stand in for Vice President Charles Curtis to announce she would seek new election in 1932. She won, becoming the first woman elected for a full term.
question.clue: This first woman to be elected to the Senate, serving from 1931 to 1945 and succeeding her husband, Thaddeus.

swap.leadin: Members of this movement, led by Walter Waters, were later appeased by the Roosevelt administration's offer of employment in the Civilian Conservation Corps.
swap.text: Name this 1932 political protest which petitioned for early payment owed to American veterans of World War I. This protest was swiftly put down with tear gas and bayonets.
swap.clue: Pelham Glassford twice reinstated Walter Waters as the leader of this group, which Gladwin Bland described as "an immense hobo jungle."

question.leadin: The millionaire James Howe established a Madison Street college for these people where professors from the University of Chicago and Northwestern taught.
question.text: Name these people who popularized "mulligan stew" during the Great Depression.
question.clue: John Hodgman's The Areas of My Expertise includes matters pertaining to this group right after cryptozoology in its subtitle and provides a list of 700 names of people bearing this designation.

swap.text: This man was the last American appointed governor of Puerto Rico. As part of FDR's brain trust, he helped create the AAA and the Resettlement Administration.
swap.clue: In another role, this man was influenced by the ideas of Clarence Perry and Clarence Stein in trying to design three thousand self-sufficient communities while working with John Lansill, those communities being known as Greenbelt Towns.

question.leadin: Answer the following about union busting in America in 1937.
question.text: The Memorial Day Massacre during the 1937 Little Steel strike was investigated by this Senate Committee on labor rights, which was chaired by the son of a third-party presidential candidate who ran with Burton K. Wheeler.
question.answerHtml: La Follette Committee [or La Follette Civil Liberties Committee] (It was chaired by “Young Bob,” the son of Robert M. La Follette.)

swap.text: This then-cabinet member was put in charge of relief efforts, and formed the Colored Advisory Committee led by Robert Moton to burnish his reputation among African-Americans.
swap.clue: As head of the Food Administration during World War I, this future President advocated for "Wheatless Wednesdays" and "Meatless Mondays."

question.text: The "Special Committee" that preceded HUAC investigated this supposed fascist-industrialist plan to overthrow FDR, which was revealed when the awesomely named Smedley Butler claimed that Gerald MacGuire tried to hire him to stage a coup d'etat.
question.answerHtml: the Business Plot [accept White House Putsch; prompt on Plot Against FDR or equivalents]
question.clue: Robert Clark employed one man involved in this incident, the only conspirator to testify before the McCormack-Dickstein committee.

swap.leadin: Name these 20th-century pieces of antitrust legislation, FTP each.
swap.text: The next major piece of antitrust legislation was this 1936 bill that explicitly defined the forms of price discrimination that the Clayton Act forbid.
swap.clue: An amendment to Section 2 of the Clayton Antitrust Act, it made it illegal to sell goods at different prices to distributors in order to reduce competition.
